He played for 15 seasons, primarily with the [[Dallas Mavericks]] and [[Brooklyn Nets|New Jersey Nets]]. Harris attended the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]] and was selected with the fifth pick in the [[2004 NBA draft]] by the [[Washington Wizards]]. He was an NBA All-Star with the Nets in 2009. He was hired by [[Bally Sports Southwest]] following his retirement from the NBA. ==Early life== Harris was born and raised in [[Milwaukee]], Wisconsin; the son of Terry and Julie Harris. Throughout high school, Harris was a superior athlete and took up [[basketball]] and [[volleyball]] at [[Wauwatosa East High School]]. He played volleyball for only one season, a season in which he gained all-conference honors, before he set that aside to focus on basketball. Harris was nagged by injuries after his [[wiktionary:sophomore|sophomore]] year of high school and was unable to participate in the summer basketball camps and tournaments that are ever important in the recruiting process. Harris exploded his senior season at Wauwatosa East in 2001, setting school scoring records through an undefeated regular season. Harris was named Wisconsin's "Mr. Basketball" for 2001, edging out [[Travis Diener]] of [[Fond du Lac High School]]. Harris finally accepted an offer to play for [[Dick Bennett]] at the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]]. Bennett retired in the midst of the upcoming season and by the time Harris arrived on campus, [[Bo Ryan]] was the head coach. Harris's number 20 jersey was retired by Wauwatosa East at ceremonies held in 2007.Witrado, Anthony. [http://www.jsonline.com/story/index.aspx?id=564643 "Tosa East gives Harris, Smith high honor"], ''[[Milwaukee Journal Sentinel]]'', February 12, 2007. Retrieved December 30, 2007. "But before Harris played basketball at the University of Wisconsin or for the Dallas Mavericks, he wowed fans, coaches and even opposing players at Wauwatosa East." ==College career== In Harris's freshman season, the [[2001–02 Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball team|2001–02 season]], he was a starter on an unheralded team. The Badgers came into the season being predicted to finish as low as ninth in the [[Big Ten Conference]] (which had eleven teams at the time). On a team led by seniors Charlie Wills and Travon Davis, the Badgers won an unexpected Big Ten Championship (shared with three other teams: [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]], [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois]], and [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State]]). Harris's sophomore season was his "breakout" year. Harris, along with senior [[Kirk Penney]] and fellow sophomore [[Mike Wilkinson (basketball)|Mike Wilkinson]], led the Badgers to their second consecutive Big Ten Championship. In the [[NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]], the Badgers reached the "Sweet 16". In the Sweet 16 game against [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]], Harris showcased his skill before a national audience, despite an eventual Badger loss. The [[2003–04 Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball team|2003–04 season]] saw Harris establish himself as one of the top players in the nation. Harris was the leader on the team and was considered a "coach on the floor" by [[Bo Ryan]].[http://www.enquirer.com/editions/2004/01/10/spt_spthoop1a.html Tipoff: Around the nation] He garnered several awards, including [[Big Ten Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Big Ten Player of the Year]], [[2004 Big Ten men's basketball tournament]] [[Big Ten tournament Most Outstanding Player|MOP]], the [[Silver Basketball]] award, and was named a Second Team All-American. Harris decided to leave college early after his junior year to play in the [[NBA]]. ==NBA career== ===Draft day=== Days prior to the draft, the [[Washington Wizards]] and [[Dallas Mavericks]] agreed to a deal that involved the Wizards' 5th overall pick going to the Mavs along with [[Jerry Stackhouse]] and [[Christian Laettner]] in exchange for [[Antawn Jamison]]. NBA rules prevented teams from trading draft picks for two consecutive years (in addition to trade kicker details in Laettner's contract{{Cite web |last=Stein |first=Marc |date=June 24, 2004 |title=Sources: Mavs deal Jamison for No. 5 overall pick |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=1827125 |access-date=2025-04-08 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press}}) so the deal was momentarily delayed until the actual draft in which Washington selected Harris and subsequently traded him to the Mavericks to complete the deal. The Mavs' plan was to bring Harris along slowly under the tutelage of all-star point guard [[Steve Nash]] but Nash ended up leaving the team through free agency and signing with the [[Phoenix Suns]].{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/mavericks/news/donnie_nelsons_comments062404.html |title=Mavericks: Donnie Nelson's Comments on Draft Picks |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=September 6, 2006 |archive-date=August 30, 2005 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050830064006/http://www.nba.com/mavericks/news/donnie_nelsons_comments062404.html |url-status=dead }} ===Dallas Mavericks (2004–2008)=== In Harris's rookie season, he averaged 5.7 points and 2.2 assist per game, but put up a [[Player efficiency rating|PER]] of 14.69. He ranked 2nd in the NBA in steals per 48 minutes at 3.15 (behind [[Larry Hughes]]), and in November 2004 was named the Rookie of the Month. Although he started for much of the early portion of the season, his playing time dwindled as the season progressed. Harris showed marked improvement in the early stages of the [[2005–06 NBA season|2005–06 season]], especially when it came to scoring; as a result, his minutes increased and he took more ball-handling responsibilities from [[Jason Terry]]. He is known for his exceptional speed, earning comparisons to other NBA guards like the [[Phoenix Suns]]' [[Leandro Barbosa]] and his good friend, the [[Miami Heat]]'s [[Dwyane Wade]]. He ended the year with averages of 9.9 points and 3.2 assists per game. He improved his jump-shot and his ability to split defenses and get to the rim. Midway through the year, he sustained a leg injury and missed most of the rest of the regular season. Harris returned for the [[2006 NBA playoffs|playoffs]] and played a huge role in toppling the Mavericks' longtime rivals, the [[San Antonio Spurs]]. The Spurs had dominated the Mavs in recent playoff history, ending their playoff runs in 6 games in [[2003 NBA playoffs|2003]] and 5 games in [[2001 NBA playoffs|2001]]. Devin Harris and the Mavericks reached the 2006 NBA Finals, where they lost to the Miami Heat 4 games to 2. In the [[2006–07 NBA season|2006–07 season]], Harris averaged 10.2 points, 2.5 rebounds, and 3.7 assists per game. After becoming the starting point guard for the Mavericks in the 2006–07 season, he helped lead the Mavericks to a team record of 67 wins in the regular season only to be upset by the eighth-seeded [[Golden State Warriors]] in the [[2007 NBA playoffs|2007 playoffs]]. Halfway through the [[2007–08 NBA season|2007–08 season]], Harris was averaging career highs with 14.4 points per game and 5.4 assists per game. He was named a co-captain in 2007–08 along with [[Dirk Nowitzki]]. ===New Jersey Nets (2008–2011)=== [[File:Devin Harris Nets 2009 (cropped).jpg|thumb|upright|Harris with the Nets in 2009]] On February 19, 2008, he was traded to the [[Brooklyn Nets|New Jersey Nets]] with [[Keith Van Horn]], [[Trenton Hassell]], [[DeSagana Diop]], [[Maurice Ager]], $3 million cash and two first-round draft picks (2008, 2010) in exchange for [[Jason Kidd]], [[Malik Allen]], and [[Antoine Wright (basketball)|Antoine Wright]].{{cite web |title=Nets acquire Devin Harris and two first round draft picks in eight player trade with Dallas |url=http://www.nba.com/nets/news/Harris_trade_release_2_19_08.html |website=NBA.com |access-date=April 22, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081219172603/http://www.nba.com/nets/news/Harris_trade_release_2_19_08.html |archive-date=December 19, 2008 |date=February 19, 2008}} In his Nets home game debut against the [[Milwaukee Bucks]], he posted 21 points and five assists in just under 21 minutes. Towards the end of the game he was treated to chants of "Dev-in Harris! Dev-in Harris!", and the first 5,000 attendees received Harris T-shirts in the Nets' next home game versus the [[San Antonio Spurs]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/280228017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241222052119/https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/280228017|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 22, 2024|title=Bucks 106-120 Nets (Feb 28, 2008) Game Recap|website=ESPN}} After New Jersey missed the playoffs for the first time in 7 years, he expressed that he was not satisfied with the way he played toward the season's end and he said he would mainly need to work on his assertiveness on offense over the summer. On November 7, 2008, Harris posted a career-high 38 points against [[NBA All-Star Game|All-Star]] [[Allen Iverson]], who was making his debut with the [[Detroit Pistons]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/281107017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241222053034/https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/281107017|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 22, 2024|title=Pistons 96-103 Nets (Nov 7, 2008) Game Recap|website=ESPN}} He later bettered that mark on November 30 with 47 points, including scoring 21 in both the first half and the fourth quarter, against the [[Phoenix Suns|Suns]] in the Nets' first win in [[Phoenix, Arizona|Phoenix]] since 1993.{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/281130021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240724222612/https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/281130021|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 24, 2024|title=Nets 117-109 Suns (Nov 30, 2008) Game Recap|website=ESPN}} On December 19, in [[Dallas Mavericks|Dallas]]'s first game at the Nets' [[Izod Center]] since the trade between the two teams, Harris put on a masterful performance posting 41 points and a season-high 13 assists in a blowout victory against his former team, while outplaying the player for whom he was essentially traded, [[Jason Kidd]]. Towards the end of the game, Nets fans were chanting "Thank you Cuban!" (Mavericks team owner [[Mark Cuban]] was sitting courtside).{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/281219017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241222052109/https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/281219017|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 22, 2024|title=Mavericks 97-121 Nets (Dec 19, 2008) Game Recap|website=ESPN}} On January 29, 2009, Harris was named a reserve for the [[2009 NBA All-Star Game]]. It was the first and only time Harris was named as an All-Star in his career.{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3870364|title=Hornets' West an All-Star; voters snub Carmelo|date=January 29, 2009|website=ESPN.com}} On February 23, 2009, in a game against the 76ers, Harris converted a half-court buzzer-beating 47-foot shot, known as "the Harris Heave," to win the game 98–96.{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20090223/PHINJN/recap.html |title=Harris makes "miracle" shot, gives Nets win |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=March 2, 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090312055043/http://www.nba.com/games/20090223/PHINJN/recap.html |archive-date=March 12, 2009 |url-status=dead }} In a cost-cutting move, the Nets traded [[Vince Carter]] on the same day of the [[2009 NBA draft]], leaving Harris to assume the role of team captain. Harris was out for large portions of the season with shoulder and ankle injuries, including the team's infamous 0–18 start. His personal play, stats, and talent around him were well below the previous year but he managed to bring his averages back up to just under 17 points per game and 6 assists per game. In order to reduce his risk of injury, Harris took part in a weight training program during the summer of 2010 at Nets' head coach (and Harris's former head coach in Dallas) [[Avery Johnson]]'s request. He managed to add 15 pounds of muscle and also worked on his defense with Tim Grover. ===Utah Jazz (2011–2012)=== On February 23, 2011, Harris was traded along with rookie [[Derrick Favors]], two draft picks and $3 million cash to the [[Utah Jazz]] in exchange for [[Deron Williams]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=6150419|title=Nets trade for Jazz All-Star PG Williams|date=February 23, 2011|website=ESPN.com}} ===Atlanta Hawks (2012–2013)=== On July 11, 2012, Harris was traded to the [[Atlanta Hawks]] for [[Marvin Williams]].{{cite web | url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/two-major-transactions-significantly-reshape-hawks-future | title=Two major transactions significantly reshape Hawks future | publisher=National Basketball Association | date=July 11, 2012 | access-date=October 30, 2020}} ===Return to Dallas (2013–2018)=== [[File:Devin Harris 2014-01-04.jpg|thumb|Harris in 2014]] In early July 2013, it was widely reported that Harris would return to his original team, the [[Dallas Mavericks]].{{cite web|url=http://www.cbssports.com/nba/eye-on-basketball/22665609/reports-devin-harris-agrees-to-three-year-deal-with-dallas|title=Reports: Devin Harris agrees to three-year deal with Dallas|work=CBS Sports|last=Young|first=Royce|date=July 7, 2013|access-date=February 21, 2016}} However, the deal was later rescinded after it was discovered that Harris required surgery for a toe injury.{{cite news|url=http://www.cbssports.com/nba/eye-on-basketball/22735897/report-mavericks-deal-with-devin-harris-scrapped-over-injury|title=Report: Mavericks' deal with Devin Harris scrapped over injury|work=CBSSports.com|last=Moore|first=Matt|date=July 7, 2013|access-date=February 21, 2016}} Despite the injury concerns, Mavericks owner [[Mark Cuban]] expressed his intention to reunite with Harris, stating that he'd be returning to the team following a restructured deal,{{cite web|url=http://fansided.com/2013/07/18/devin-harris-will-return-to-dallas-mavericks/|title=Devin Harris Will Return to Dallas Mavericks|work=FanSided.com|last=Rose|first=Bryan|date=July 18, 2013|access-date=July 18, 2013}} and on July 31, Harris signed with the Mavericks to a one-year, $1.3 million contract.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/dallas/nba/story/_/id/9526228|title=Devin Harris gets veteran's minimum|publisher=ESPN|last=MacMahon|first=Tim|date=July 31, 2013|access-date=October 30, 2020}} On January 18, 2014, Harris made his season debut and scored six points in 17 minutes off the bench in the Mavericks' 127–111 loss to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20140118/PORDAL/gameinfo.html|title=Notebook: Trail Blazers 127, Mavericks 111|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=January 18, 2014|access-date=January 26, 2014}} He played well off the bench for the Mavericks over the second half of the 2013–14 season, scoring a season-high 20 points on March 9 in a win over the [[Indiana Pacers]]. His performance off the bench during the Mavericks' first-round series loss to the [[San Antonio Spurs]] was impressive, scoring over 17 points in three of the series' seven games.{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/h/harride01/gamelog/2014/|title=Devin Harris 2013–14 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=February 21, 2016}} On July 17, 2014, Harris re-signed with the Mavericks to a four-year, $16.5 million contract.{{cite web|url=http://www.mavs.com/mavericks-re-sign-devin-harris/|title=Mavericks Re-Sign Devin Harris|work=Mavs.com|date=July 17, 2014|access-date=July 17, 2014}}{{cite web|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/2014/07/17/mavericks-officially-re-sign-g-devin-harris/12815083/|title=Mavericks officially re-sign G Devin Harris|work=USA Today|date=July 17, 2014|access-date=July 17, 2014}} Harris entered the 2014–15 season as the team's wily veteran and was much healthier than he had been the previous year, and it showed. He missed just six games all season, providing a constant spark off the bench behind [[Rajon Rondo]] and [[Monta Ellis]]. In the team's fourth last game of the season on April 10, Harris scored a season-high 21 points against the [[Denver Nuggets]]. He went on to play in four of the Mavericks' five first-round playoff games against the [[Houston Rockets]]. His 2014 playoff form did not follow over to 2015, though, as he scored in double figures in just one game and shot 8-of-23 from the field in the 4–1 series loss.{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/h/harride01/gamelog/2015/|title=Devin Harris 2014–15 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=February 21, 2016}} Harris played in 40 of the team's first 46 games to begin the 2015–16 season, averaging 7.4 points per game off the bench. A left big toe strain suffered in late January forced him out of action for 10 games, returning to the line-up on February 21 against the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160221/PHIDAL/gameinfo.html|title=Mavericks cruise to 129–103 win over 76ers|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=February 21, 2016|access-date=February 21, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160222221102/http://www.nba.com/games/20160221/PHIDAL/gameinfo.html|archive-date=February 22, 2016|url-status=dead}} On October 26, 2016, Harris was ruled out for the first three weeks of the 2016–17 season after he sprained his right big toe during preseason.{{cite web|last=Sefko|first=Eddie|url=http://sportsday.dallasnews.com/dallas-mavericks/mavericks/2016/10/26/devin-harris-least-three-weeks-will-walking-boot|title=Devin Harris out at least three weeks, will be in a walking boot|work=The Dallas Morning News|date=October 26, 2016|access-date=October 26, 2016}} He made his season debut on November 30, 2016, against the San Antonio Spurs after missing the first 16 games.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899722|title=Mills helps Spurs rally to beat Mavericks 94–87|publisher=ESPN|date=November 30, 2016|access-date=October 30, 2020}} ===Denver Nuggets (2018)=== On February 8, 2018, Harris was acquired by the [[Denver Nuggets]] in a three-team trade that also involved the Mavericks and the [[New York Knicks]], in which [[Doug McDermott]] was sent to the Mavericks and [[Emmanuel Mudiay]] was sent to the Knicks.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-acquire-harris-second-round-pick-020818|title=Nuggets Acquire Devin Harris and 2018 Second Round Pick|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=February 8, 2018|access-date=February 8, 2018}} On March 6, 2018, in a 118–107 loss to the Mavericks, Harris reached 10,000 points for his career.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975707|title=Ferrell, Nowitzki lead Mavericks to 118–107 win over Nuggets|publisher=ESPN|date=March 6, 2018|access-date=March 6, 2018}} ===Third stint with Dallas (2018–2019)=== On August 8, 2018, Harris signed with the [[Dallas Mavericks]], returning to the franchise for a third stint.{{cite web|title=Mavericks sign Devin Harris|url=https://www.mavs.com/mavericks-sign-devin-harris/|website=Mavs.com|access-date=August 8, 2018|date=August 8, 2018}} He missed 10 games early in the season with a left hamstring strain.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070942|title=Barnes scores season-high 28 as Mavericks beat Nets 119–113|publisher=ESPN|date=November 21, 2018|access-date=November 21, 2018}} On November 28, Harris led ([[Luka Dončić]] also scored 20 points) the Mavericks in scoring with a season high 20 points, in a 128–108 win over the [[Houston Rockets]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401070990|title = Mavericks vs. Rockets – Game Recap – November 28, 2018 – ESPN}} Harris's final NBA game was played on April 10, 2019, in a 94–105 loss to the [[San Antonio Spurs]]. In his final game, Harris recorded 12 points, 2 rebounds and 4 assists as the Mavs' starting point guard. This game was also Harris' teammate [[Dirk Nowitzki]]'s final NBA game. == Broadcast career == Harris is currently a MavsTV analyst covering the Dallas Mavericks, a position he started when they were on [[Bally Sports Southwest]], and has also worked for [[Fox Sports]] covering college basketball.{{Cite web |last=Kuwana |first=Claire |date=2023-03-14 |title=March Madness 2022-23: How to Watch Your
